subject: How would I specify 'latent variable 1' ~ 'latent variable 2' in a lavaan model?

messages.author: 6e39f348b9c4ff4c
messages.subject: How would I specify 'latent variable 1' ~ 'latent variable 2' in a lavaan model?
parts:
Hello all,

I am sorry for bothering you about a relatively simple question, but I have a sem model that I am working with where 2- 3 manifest variables create each of the four latent variables, and one latent variable predicts the other one. Here is some of my code:

model<-'f1 =~ t1.week.fear + t1.year.fear
            d1 =~ t1.week.depressed + t1.month.depressed + t1.week.sad
            f1 =~ t2.week.fear + t2.often.fear
            d2 =~ t2.week.depressed + t2.week.sad
            t1.week.fear ~~ t2.week.fear
            t1.week.depressed ~~ t2.week.depressed
            t1.week.sad ~~ t2.week.sad
            f2 ~ f1
            d2 ~ d1'

fit.path <-lavaan(model, data=dt, fixed.x=FALSE)

Upon executing this, I receive the error: Error in `[.data.frame`(data, , unlist(ov.names)) : undefined columns selected
This seems to be related to the last two terms in the model (f2 ~ f1 and d2 ~ d1) because when I remove them, the model runs just fine.

Is there a way to specify that f1, f2, d1, and d2 are not manifest variables so lavaan uses information in the model instead of information in the column headings?

Thank you so much for sharing your knowledge and expertise!

-Xander
